How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide to build the **GET** request you’ll send to the Cisco Nexus Dashboard (ND) API to retrieve the *Speed* information for a specific interface. | Item | Value | |------|-------| | **Base URL** | `https://192.120.45.67` | | **Endpoint** | `/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo` | | **Query Parameters** | `fabricName=Network1`
`nodeId=12`
`podId=10`
`interfaceType=ethernet`
`infoType=Speed` | > **Note** > * `interfaceType` must be one of the accepted values: `gigabitethernet`, `fastethernet`, `ethernet`, or `serial`. > * `infoType` can be `statistics`, `status`, `config`, or `Speed`. --- ## 1. Construct the full URL ```text https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed ``` --- ## 2. Authentication The ND API typically requires a bearer token (or basic auth). If you’re using a token: ```bash export ND_TOKEN="YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN" ``` --- ## 3. Example Requests ### a) Using `curl` ```bash curl -k \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ND_TOKEN" \ "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo?fabricName=Network1&nodeId=12&podId=10&interfaceType=ethernet&infoType=Speed" ``` * `-k` – skip certificate verification (use only in dev/test). * Replace `$ND_TOKEN` with your actual token. ### b) Using Python `requests` ```python import requests url = "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo" params = { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } headers = { "Authorization": f"Bearer {ND_TOKEN}" } response = requests.get(url, params=params, headers=headers, verify=False) print(response.status_code) print(response.json()) ``` > **Tip:** If you’re running this in a production environment, set `verify=True` and provide the proper CA bundle. --- ## 4. Expected Response A successful call will return JSON similar to: ```json { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed", "speedMbps": 1000 } ``` (Actual field names may vary; consult the ND API docs for the exact schema.) --- ## 5. Using the Provided Function (Optional) If you want to invoke the request programmatically via the helper function defined in the toolset: ```python from functions import requests_get result = requests_get({ "url": "https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo", "params": { "fabricName": "Network1", "nodeId": 12, "podId": 10, "interfaceType": "ethernet", "infoType": "Speed" } }) print(result) ``` > **Important:** The helper function will automatically handle the HTTP call; you still need to supply any required authentication headers if the function wrapper does not do so. --- ### Quick Checklist | ✅ | Item | |---|------| | ✅ | Base URL + endpoint | | ✅ | Query parameters (fabricName, nodeId, podId, interfaceType, infoType) | | ✅ | Authorization header (Bearer token) | | ✅ | HTTPS (verify SSL) | | ✅ | Correct HTTP method (`GET`) | That’s all you need to generate and execute a RESTful API request to fetch the interface speed from Cisco Nexus Dashboard. Happy querying!
